Carbon capture and storage is an environmental technology designed to help tackle climate change. It aims to reduce the amount of carbon dioxide (CO₂) released into the atmosphere by industrial activities. The process starts by capturing CO₂ emissions at their source, such as a power plant or factory, before they are released into the air. This is important because CO₂, when released, can worsen global warming by trapping heat in the Earth's atmosphere. Once collected, the CO₂ is compressed and transported to suitable storage sites where it is securely stored underground or in geological formations. This prevents the CO₂ from entering the atmosphere and contributing to global warming. The storage sites are carefully selected and monitored to ensure the safety and effectiveness of the carbon capture process. This innovative approach plays an important role in lowering the amount of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. Nonetheless, this technology is still in its early stages of development, and it alone is not enough to solve the climate crisis. It must be accompanied by other measures, such as transitioning to renewable energy sources and increasing energy efficiency, to really make a difference in global carbon levels.

Have you heard of the right to be forgotten? This means individuals have the right to request that their private information be removed from the internet under certain circumstances. In 2014, a Spanish lawyer sued a global search engine company because he didn't want people to see old articles about him. He argued that since he had already solved his issues in the past, the articles should be deleted. The European Court ruled that information can be removed if it isn't accurate or relevant anymore. However, in my opinion, it's more important to consider the individuals who have been harmed by information they want others to forget. I believe everyone should have control over their own privacy.

Carbon capture and storage is an environmental technology designed to help tackle climate change. It aims to reduce the amount of carbon dioxide (CO₂) released into the atmosphere by industrial activities. The process starts by capturing CO₂ emissions at their source, such as a power plant or factory, before they are released into the air. This is important because CO₂, when released, can worsen global warming by trapping heat in the Earth's atmosphere. Once collected, the CO₂ is compressed and transported to suitable storage sites where it is securely stored underground or in geological formations. This prevents the CO₂ from entering the atmosphere and contributing to global warming. The storage sites are carefully selected and monitored to ensure the safety and effectiveness of the carbon capture process. This innovative approach plays an important role in lowering the amount of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. Nonetheless, this technology is still in its early stages of development, and it alone is not enough to solve the climate crisis. It must be accompanied by other measures, such as transitioning to renewable energy sources and increasing energy efficiency, to really make a difference in global carbon levels.

Carbon capture and storage is an environmental technology designed to help tackle climate change. It aims to reduce the amount of carbon dioxide (CO₂) released into the atmosphere by industrial activities. The process starts by capturing CO₂ emissions at their source, such as a power plant or factory, before they are released into the air. This is important because CO₂, when released, can worsen global warming by trapping heat in the Earth's atmosphere. Once collected, the CO₂ is compressed and transported to suitable storage sites where it is securely stored underground or in geological formations. This prevents the CO₂ from entering the atmosphere and contributing to global warming. The storage sites are carefully selected and monitored to ensure the safety and effectiveness of the carbon capture process. This innovative approach plays an important role in lowering the amount of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. Nonetheless, this technology is still in its early stages of development, and it alone is not enough to solve the climate crisis. It must be accompanied by other measures, such as transitioning to renewable energy sources and increasing energy efficiency, to really make a difference in global carbon levels.
